content:
In August, Fender launched the MIX wireless headphones priced at US$299. These over-ear headphones come with replaceable batteries and a FWD Tx USB-C wireless transmitter, enabling low-latency, lossless connection. The Fender MIX headphones now also support an iPhone app, allowing users to customise their listening experience.

The Fender Audio iPhone app offers EQ presets and a customisable five-band equaliser, allowing you to separately adjust bass, low mids, mids, high mids and treble. Users can directly adjust the sound to their preferences within the iPhone app.

The app also includes a battery indicator and customisable home screen widgets, allowing quick access to various functions including EQ settings.

As for the headphones themselves, the MIX features 40mm graphene drivers, hybrid active noise cancellation, and Bluetooth 5.3. Fender claims up to 52 hours of battery life with ANC (active noise cancellation) on, and up to 100 hours with ANC off.

The included USB-C transmitter supports multiple modes, including lossless audio up to 24-bit/96kHz, low-latency listening, and Auracast functionality for broadcasting to multiple compatible devices.

The headphones also support wired listening via USB-C or a 3.5mm audio cable.

Based on my brief listening experience so far, the MIX delivers decent sound quality when active noise cancellation is engaged. Switching to Ambient Sound mode — Fender's transparency mode — the audio quality seems to dip somewhat to my ears, at least when relying on Bluetooth alone without the dongle.

I'm looking forward to trying out the EQ controls in the app to see whether I can tune the sound closer to my personal preference.

The USB-C transmitter can be neatly stored behind the ear cushions when not in use, and when convenience matters more than sound specs, you can simply connect via Bluetooth without the dongle.

The Fender Audio app is now available on the App Store, supporting the Fender MIX headphones.
